name: Dindigul Chicken Biryani
cuisine: Dindigul, Tamil Nadu (Thalappakatti-style, seeraga samba rice)

ingredients.name: Shallots (small onions, sambar onion, chinna vengayam)

equipment: Heavy-bottomed pot with a tight lid (1.5–2 L), or the body of a 1.5 L pressure cooker
Mortar and pestle for the spice paste
Sieve or colander for rinsing the rice
Small bowls, a chopping board and knife
Measuring spoons and a small kitchen scale (spoon measures are given for the scale-less)
Wooden spoon or flat spatula (a metal one breaks the short grains)

steps.title: Measure the rice
steps.text: Put 80 g seeraga samba rice (6 tbsp) in a bowl.
steps.visualCue: Tiny, short, pale grains that look like cumin seeds, no stones or husk
steps.cameraCheck: The rice in the bowl
steps.videoShot: Rice poured into a bowl.
steps.watchOut: Basmati grains by mistake (long and thin); they need different water. If you only have basmati, see the rice note in section 1 and use a little less water.
steps.funFact: Seeraga samba is named for its resemblance to cumin seeds ("seeragam" is cumin in Tamil).

steps.title: Rinse the rice
steps.text: Put the rice in a sieve and rinse under cold water, swirling with your fingers, 2 times.
steps.visualCue: Water runs from cloudy to nearly clear
steps.cameraCheck: The rinsed rice in the sieve
steps.videoShot: Water running over rice in a sieve.
steps.watchOut: Rubbing hard; the short grains snap. Swirl gently and stop when the water is only faintly cloudy.

steps.title: Soak the rice
steps.text: Put the rinsed rice in a bowl, cover with water and leave for 20 min.
steps.tip: Set a phone timer so you do not forget the rice.
steps.visualCue: Grains turn from translucent to chalky white and swell slightly
steps.cameraCheck: The rice covered with water
steps.videoShot: A timer set to 20 min beside the bowl of rice.
steps.watchOut: Soaking longer than 30 min; the grains go soft and break in the pot (the research sources range from 15 to 30 min; this recipe uses 20). If you forgot and it has been over an hour, drain it and use 10 ml less water.

steps.title: Measure the chicken
steps.text: Put 170 g bone-in skinless chicken pieces in a bowl and pat dry with paper.
steps.visualCue: Pink-white pieces, no skin, no pooled liquid
steps.cameraCheck: The chicken in the bowl
steps.videoShot: Chicken pieces patted dry with paper.
steps.watchOut: Wet chicken waters down the marinade and the masala stays pale. Pat it dry; if it smells sour or looks slimy, do not use it.

steps.title: Add the marinade
steps.text: Add 1 heaped tbsp (20 g) curd, ¼ tsp turmeric, ½ tsp lemon juice and a generous ¼ tsp (1 g) salt to the chicken.
steps.visualCue: A thin, pale-yellow coating over every piece
steps.cameraCheck: The bowl with curd and spices on the chicken
steps.videoShot: A spoon turning chicken in yellow curd.
steps.watchOut: Dry spots on some pieces. Turn each piece over with a spoon until nothing is left uncoated.

steps.title: Marinate the chicken
steps.text: Cover the bowl and leave for 20 min, in the fridge if the day is hot.
steps.visualCue: The curd looks absorbed and the chicken is evenly yellow
steps.cameraCheck: The covered bowl
steps.videoShot: The bowl being covered and placed on the counter.
steps.watchOut: Leaving it out of the fridge for more than 30 min on a hot day. Put it in the fridge; you can marinate up to a few hours ahead.

steps.title: Peel and slice the shallots
steps.text: Peel 8–10 small shallots (60 g) and slice them thinly.
steps.visualCue: Thin, even slices, about 1 mm thick
steps.cameraCheck: The sliced shallots on the board
steps.videoShot: A knife slicing a peeled shallot.
steps.watchOut: Uneven thick and thin slices; the thin ones burn while the thick ones stay raw. Slice them as even as you can; if your eyes sting, chill the shallots for 10 min first.

steps.title: Prepare the ginger, garlic and chilli
steps.text: Peel and roughly chop 5 g ginger (1 cm) and 6 g garlic (2 cloves), and cut 6 g green chilli (1–2) into rings.
steps.tip: Remove the chilli seeds for less heat.
steps.visualCue: Small pieces, ready to crush; ginger pale yellow, chilli green
steps.cameraCheck: The three prepared items together
steps.videoShot: Garlic cloves crushed under a knife.
steps.watchOut: Chilli on your fingers. Do not touch your eyes, and wash your hands with soap straight away; if they still burn, rub a little oil on them first and then wash.

steps.title: Grind the whole spices
steps.text: In a mortar, grind 2 cloves, 2 cardamom pods, 1 cm cinnamon and 1 blade of mace coarsely, without water.
steps.visualCue: A coarse brown powder with a sweet, warm smell
steps.cameraCheck: The ground spices in the mortar
steps.videoShot: A pestle crushing cloves and cinnamon.
steps.watchOut: Grinding it fine or adding water at this stage; the spice flavour turns dull. Stop while there are still small flecks, and remove any big cardamom husk pieces.
steps.funFact: Dindigul-style biryani gets its flavour from whole spices ground fresh, not from ready-made garam masala (Vidhya's Home Cooking).

steps.title: Make the spice paste
steps.text: Add the ginger, garlic and green chilli to the mortar and crush into a coarse paste, adding 1 tsp water only if it will not come together.
steps.visualCue: A thick, rough green-brown paste, with no whole garlic left
steps.cameraCheck: The paste in the mortar
steps.videoShot: The pestle working the paste against the side of the mortar.
steps.watchOut: A watery paste; it will steam instead of fry in step 14. Add the water only a few drops at a time.

steps.title: Chop the herbs
steps.text: Roughly chop 2 tbsp (5 g) mint leaves and 2 tbsp (5 g) coriander leaves.
steps.visualCue: Rough bright-green pieces
steps.cameraCheck: The chopped herbs
steps.videoShot: A knife rocking over mint and coriander.
steps.watchOut: Chopping too early; the herbs blacken if left cut for long. Chop them right before step 15.

steps.title: Heat the oil and ghee
steps.text: Put the pot on medium heat. Add 1 tsp (5 ml) oil and 1½ tsp (7 g) ghee.
steps.visualCue: The ghee melts and the fat shimmers, with a light nutty smell
steps.cameraCheck: The shimmering fat in the pot
steps.videoShot: Ghee melting into oil.
steps.watchOut: Smoke or a burnt smell, a sign it is too hot. Take the pot off the heat for 20 seconds, lower the flame, and start again with fresh fat if it has turned dark.

steps.title: Cook the shallots
steps.text: Add the sliced shallots and cook, stirring every 30 seconds.
steps.visualCue: The shallots turn soft and translucent, then light golden at the edges, with a sweet smell
steps.cameraCheck: The golden shallots in the pot
steps.videoShot: Shallots softening in the fat.
steps.watchOut: Dark-brown or crisp shallots, as in Hyderabadi biryani; they turn the biryani bitter and dark. If the edges brown within 2 minutes, lower the heat and add 1 tbsp water.

steps.title: Fry the spice paste
steps.text: Add the ginger-garlic-chilli paste and the ground spices; stir and cook.
steps.visualCue: The raw garlic smell goes and the paste darkens slightly; the fat begins to show at the edges
steps.cameraCheck: The fragrant paste in the shallots
steps.videoShot: A spoon stirring the green-brown paste.
steps.watchOut: Garlic sticking and burning on the bottom (a sharp, bitter smell). Stir constantly and add 1 tbsp water if it sticks; it recovers.

steps.title: Add the herbs
steps.text: Add the chopped mint and coriander and stir.
steps.visualCue: A strong fresh mint smell and herbs that wilt and turn a deeper green
steps.cameraCheck: The pot with herbs stirred in
steps.videoShot: Herbs dropped into the pot.
steps.watchOut: Cooking the herbs for more than a minute; they lose their freshness and go dull. Add the chicken immediately after.

steps.title: Add the chicken
steps.text: Add the marinated chicken with all the marinade, raise the heat to medium-high and stir.
steps.visualCue: The pink colour fades to opaque white on the outside, coated with a green-yellow masala
steps.cameraCheck: The chicken coated in masala
steps.videoShot: Chicken pieces turning white in the masala.
steps.watchOut: Low heat, which makes the chicken release water and boil instead of browning. Keep the heat medium-high and stir often; if the curd looks split (small curdled bits), keep stirring, because it will blend in as the water is added.

steps.title: Add the pot salt
steps.text: Sprinkle in 1.5 g salt (a scant ¼ tsp) and stir.
steps.visualCue: The masala starts to look glossy
steps.cameraCheck: The salt measured in a spoon
steps.videoShot: Salt falling into the pot.
steps.watchOut: Adding more salt now; the marinade already has 1 g, and the water you add next will dilute it. Taste after the rice is cooked, not before.

steps.title: Add the water
steps.text: Pour in ½ cup (125 ml) water, stir and bring to a rolling boil on high heat.
steps.tip: Taste the liquid; it should taste slightly too salty, because the rice will absorb some of it.
steps.visualCue: Big bubbles break all over the surface and the liquid looks light brown-green
steps.cameraCheck: The boiling liquid
steps.videoShot: Water poured into the pot, then boiling.
steps.watchOut: Too much water, which makes soft, porridge-like rice. Measure it exactly; if it looks too watery to you, keep it boiling 1–2 min uncovered before adding the rice.

steps.title: Add the rice
steps.text: Drain the soaked rice well and add it to the boiling liquid. Level it with the back of the spoon and do not stir again.
steps.visualCue: The rice sits just under or at the surface of the liquid, in an even layer
steps.cameraCheck: The level rice in the pot
steps.videoShot: Rice slid into the pot and levelled.
steps.watchOut: Stirring hard, which breaks the grains and makes them sticky. Stir once gently to spread it, then leave it. If the water is far below the rice (it should just cover or reach the rice), add 2 tbsp hot water.

steps.title: Cover and cook
steps.text: Reduce to the lowest flame, cover with the tight lid, and cook for 15 min. Do not lift the lid.
steps.tip: Put a tawa under the pot if your flame will not go very low.
steps.visualCue: Steam seeps from the edge of the lid with a spiced, nutty smell; no crackling sound
steps.cameraCheck: The covered pot on a low flame
steps.videoShot: The lid on and a thin trail of steam coming out.
steps.watchOut: A burning smell or crackling, a sign that the water has dried and the bottom is catching. Switch off at once, and leave it covered for 10 min; the steam will finish the rice.

steps.title: Rest the pot
steps.text: Switch off the heat and leave the pot covered, untouched, for 10 min.
steps.visualCue: The steam slowly stops and the lid is warm
steps.cameraCheck: The closed pot off the heat
steps.videoShot: A hand turning off the flame knob.
steps.watchOut: Opening the lid now; the grains will be wet and fall apart. Waiting lets the extra moisture spread evenly through the rice.

steps.title: Check the chicken
steps.text: Open the lid and lift out one thick chicken piece; cut it near the bone.
steps.visualCue: White meat with no pink and clear juices at the bone; it pulls easily off the bone
steps.cameraCheck: The cut piece of chicken
steps.videoShot: A knife cutting a chicken piece near the bone.
steps.watchOut: Pink meat or red juices near the bone. Put the lid back and cook on low for 5 more minutes with 2 tbsp hot water sprinkled over, then rest 5 min.

steps.title: Fluff the rice
steps.text: Slide a flat spoon from the edge to the bottom and lift the rice gently, folding the chicken through.
steps.visualCue: Separate, glossy, tender grains with no wet clumps, and shallot strands through the rice
steps.cameraCheck: The fluffed biryani in the pot
steps.videoShot: A flat spoon lifting rice with chicken pieces.
steps.watchOut: Mashing or stirring, which turns the short grains to paste. Lift and fold from the side only; if there is wet rice at the bottom, leave the pot on a very low flame, uncovered, for 1–2 min.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Put the biryani on a plate. Serve hot with plain raita and sliced onion if you like (not counted in section 5).
steps.visualCue: Pale golden-brown grains flecked with green herbs, chicken pieces on top, steam rising
steps.cameraCheck: The finished plate
steps.videoShot: Steam rising from the plated biryani.
steps.watchOut: Letting it cool in the pot with the lid on; the rice at the bottom goes soggy. Plate it within 5 min of opening.
steps.funFact: "Thalappakatti" means "turban" in Tamil; the chain is named after its founder, who wore one when he opened his biryani hotel in Dindigul in 1957 (Dindigul Thalappakatti, Wikipedia).

reasons: a filling one-pot meal with about 33 g of protein from lean skinless chicken, good selenium, niacin and B6, and shallots and fresh herbs in the base, with only 5 ml oil and 7 g ghee. Points come off for white rice (low fibre, about 4 g), sodium (about 1,100 mg), cholesterol and almost no vegetables. A restaurant plate usually has more rice, ghee and oil, skin-on pieces and a side egg and salna, and the published 163 kcal per 100 g suggests about 650 kcal for a 400 g plate.

researchRating.basis: Dindigul (Thalappakatti) biryani is one of Tamil Nadu's best-known biryani styles and the namesake chain describes itself as the largest biryani brand in India (a company press release, so treated cautiously); Swiggy's own blog lists Dindigul biryani among the town's famous foods and Swiggy's restaurant awards named the chain's Chennai outlet; home-cook blogs keep making it. Small deduction: diners' reviews on Tripadvisor are mixed, with complaints about small portions and delivery, and the dish is hard to find in Mumbai.

storage: Cool the biryani to room temperature within 1 hour (cooked rice left warm can grow Bacillus cereus), then refrigerate in a closed box for up to 2 days, or freeze for up to 1 month. Reheat only once: sprinkle 1–2 tbsp water over it, cover and warm in a pan on low for 5–7 min, or microwave covered for 2–3 min, until steaming hot all the way through. Short seeraga samba grains harden in the fridge; the water sprinkle fixes it.
leftoverRemix: biryani cutlets. Mash ½ cup of leftover biryani with the chicken shredded off the bone, 1 tbsp besan and a little chopped coriander. Shape into 3 small patties and shallow-fry in 1 tsp oil for 2–3 min per side until crisp; serve with green chutney or raita. Use within the same 2-day window.
burnOff: about 8.6 km of running (600 ÷ 70 kcal/km, for a 70 kg adult), or about 12 km of brisk walking (about 2 hours 24 minutes at 5 km/h, using about 50 kcal/km for walking) (est.).

navratri.reason: chicken, shallots and garlic are avoided, and rice is a grain most vrat rules also avoid

ekadashi.reason: meat, onion-family vegetables, garlic and rice are all avoided (common rule set: no grains)

jain.reason: chicken, shallots, garlic and fresh ginger

ramadan.reason: use halal-sourced chicken; a satisfying one-pot meal, but about 1,100 mg sodium (est.) is salty for sehri and adds to thirst

jain.reason: contains chicken, plus shallots, garlic and fresh ginger (roots)

sattvik.reason: shallots (the onion family) and garlic are the base, and the dish has chicken

glutenFree.reason: rice, chicken, curd and freshly ground whole spices; no hing, no wheat (check the label if you swap in any packaged masala)

dairyFree.reason: curd 20 g → 20 g coconut yoghurt, ghee 7 g → 7 ml oil (see Dairy-free variant)

variants.reason: the dish is defined by shallots, garlic and fresh ginger (roots) as well as chicken; a Jain biryani is a root-free vegetable biryani, a separate dish (see dish 39, Veg Biryani).
main recipe already gluten-free (rice, chicken, curd, freshly ground whole spices; no hing). Check labels on any packaged masala.
